item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 10, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Broadcasters have important deadlines ahead of the November 17 nationwide Emergency Alert System test. Sage Alerting Systems has released a mandatory firmware update, and stations installing it must amend their FCC ETRS Form One. The FCC has also issued new test preparation guidance. Get the full details at Media Jobs Report.
Turning to radio,
Cumulus Media's Z93 in Saginaw, Michigan, and Program Director Matt Bingham have raised nearly $128,000 for the American Cancer Society's Men Wear Pink campaign. A donation of more than $111,000 from two local casino partners helped place Bingham and Z93 among the nation's top five fundraisers. Over eight years, the station has raised more than $200,000 to support the fight against breast cancer.
In television news,
Gray Media has named Richard Haddox General Manager of WLIO and WOHL in Lima, Ohio, effective November 16th. Haddox brings 42 years of television experience, including 11 years leading KAUZ News Channel 6 in Wichita Falls, Texas. His broadcasting career includes leadership roles in news, production, marketing and sales.
Turning to radio,
iHeartMedia reported third-quarter revenue topping one billion dollars, up 3.3 percent from last year. Podcast revenue jumped 24 percent to 174 million dollars, while traditional broadcast radio revenue declined. The company also plans to report podcasting as a separate business segment in 2027.
In podcasting news,
Buzzsprout is making it easier to launch a podcast with its new one-dollar Podcast Starter Kit. Creators answer five simple questions and receive suggested show names, descriptions, categories and cover art. Everything is saved to their Buzzsprout account, helping new podcasters turn their ideas into shows.
Turning to radio,
Dave & Chuck the Freak are expanding to Grand Rapids! The popular morning show, originating from WRIF in Detroit, is now airing weekdays on Cumulus Media’s WLAV-FM from 6 to 10:30. Celebrating 25 years on the air, Dave, Chuck and the crew bring their signature humor and unscripted conversations to West Michigan.
And finally,
Skydance reported third-quarter revenue of $7 billion, up 5%, with Paramount+ revenue jumping 21%. The results exclude Warner Bros. Discovery, which Skydance acquired in October. The combined company plans to bundle Paramount+ and HBO Max next year while targeting $6 billion in annual cost savings.
Find more media news, jobs, industry resources and free tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
